:::{#thm-mse-consistent}
#### Vanishing population mean squared error implies consistency

If the pMSE of $\hparam_n$ goes to zero as $n$ grows,
then $\hparam_n$ is a [consistent](#def-consistent) estimator of $\param$:

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} \mselr{\hparam_n} = 0
\quad \Longrightarrow \quad
\hparam_n \inprob \param
$$ {#eq-mse-consistent}

:::

::: proof

Fix $\varepsilon > 0$.
By @lem-estimation-error-bound,
$0 \le \Prf{\abs{\hparam_n - \param} \ge \varepsilon} \le \mselr{\hparam_n} / \varepsilon^2$
for every $n$.
The upper bound goes to zero as $n \to \infty$,
because $\varepsilon$ is fixed and $\mselr{\hparam_n} \to 0$,
so the probability, squeezed between zero and the bound, goes to zero.
This holds for every $\varepsilon > 0$, which is @eq-consistent.

:::
